# Thanksgiving Hymns Column 11 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all lines in Thanksgiving Hymns Column 11 where the three translators significantly diverged, along with SOPHIA's resolution.

---

## 11:2 — "source of uncleanness" vs. "fountain of impurity" vs. "spring of filth"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "source of uncleanness" | Literal translation of Hebrew construct |
| LOGOS | "fountain of impurity" | Formal English equivalent with dignified register |
| PNEUMA | "spring of filth" | Visceral modern rendering |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS's "fountain of impurity" -- preserves the water metaphor while maintaining appropriate register. PNEUMA's "filth" is too colloquial; EMET's "uncleanness" is adequate but less vivid.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 11:6 — "reckoned" vs. "accounted" vs. "stand in Your presence"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "be reckoned before You" | Literal rendering of Hebrew verb |
| LOGOS | "be accounted before You" | Formal equivalent |
| PNEUMA | "stand in Your presence" | Dynamic rendering emphasizing the relational aspect |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS's "be accounted before You." PNEUMA's rendering loses the judicial/evaluative nuance.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 11:10 — hesed: "covenant-faithfulness" vs. "lovingkindness" vs. "faithful love"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "covenant-faithfulness" | Project convention for hesed |
| LOGOS | "lovingkindness" | Traditional formal rendering |
| PNEUMA | "faithful love" | Accessible modern equivalent |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted EMET's "covenant-faithfulness" per established project convention (see Gen 24 ruling).

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 11:15 — bene retzonekha: "sons of Your good pleasure" vs. "children of Your favor" vs. "everyone You have chosen"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "sons of Your good pleasure" | Literal: bene = sons, ratzon = good pleasure |
| LOGOS | "children of Your favor" | Formal equivalent using inclusive "children" |
| PNEUMA | "everyone You have chosen" | Dynamic simplification of sectarian term |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS's "children of Your favor" -- inclusive language without losing the theological specificity. PNEUMA's paraphrase loses the Qumran self-designation.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 11:19 — "worm of the dead" vs. "worm of mortality" vs. "worm from the grave-dust"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "worm of the dead" | Literal Hebrew construct |
| LOGOS | "worm of mortality" | Abstract formal rendering |
| PNEUMA | "worm from the grave-dust" | Vivid contextual paraphrase |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted EMET's "worm of the dead" -- most faithful to the Hebrew and sufficiently clear in context.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 11:27 — "spirit that God has formed" vs. "spirit God has shaped" vs. "God's own spirit"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "spirit that God has formed for him" | Literal: yatsar used for spirit as for clay |
| LOGOS | "spirit God has shaped for him" | Formal equivalent |
| PNEUMA | "God's own spirit steadies him" | Dynamic reinterpretation -- spirit belongs to God rather than being formed for the person |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted EMET's "spirit God has formed for him." PNEUMA's rendering changes the theology -- the text speaks of a spirit God shapes *for* the individual, not God's own spirit.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET. PNEUMA's rendering corrected.

---

## 11:31 — "water poured out on a slope" vs. "water rushing downhill" vs. "water cascading down a hillside"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "water poured out on a slope" | Literal rendering |
| LOGOS | "water rushing downhill" | Formal but slightly interpretive |
| PNEUMA | "water cascading down a hillside" | Vivid dynamic rendering |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted EMET's "water poured down a slope" (with minor adjustment) -- closest to the Hebrew image without embellishment.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET with minor adjustment.

---

## 11:35 — "strengthened myself" vs. "took courage" vs. "gathered my strength"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "I strengthened myself, and I rose" | Literal reflexive form |
| LOGOS | "I took courage" | Idiomatic formal English |
| PNEUMA | "I gathered my strength. I stood up" | Dynamic with dramatic pacing |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted a blend: "I gathered strength. I rose" -- captures the self-rallying sense while maintaining dignity and brevity.

**Status:** Resolved with composite rendering.

---

**Total disagreements for Column 11:** 8
